name: OWASP Application Security Verification Standard (ASVS)
source_notes: Verified against the official OWASP/ASVS GitHub repo, folder 5.0/en (header, frontispiece, README and chapter tables; cloned 2026-10-05).
caveats: Primary sources only say "May 2025" (released live at Global AppSec EU Barcelona 2025); the commonly cited day 2025-05-30 is unverified.
url points to the official OWASP GitHub repo; the owasp.org project page URL was not captured in the research notes.
Level counts (L1 70, L2 183, L3 92, total 345) are the researcher's count of requirement rows in the source tables, consistent with OWASP's ~20%/~50%/~30% split; not an official published figure.
l1_requirements summaries are short paraphrases. The notes label them "selected" L1 requirements, but they total 70, matching the L1 count, so the set is likely complete; unconfirmed.
No L1 requirements were found in V16 (Security Logging and Error Handling) or V17 (WebRTC); V13 secret-management requirements (13.3.x) are L2+ and only 13.4.1 is L1 in V13.
10.4.3 (authorization code lifetime) applies at L1/L2 per the notes; 10.4.x L1 items are authorization-server-side.
ASVS 5.0 chapter numbering differs heavily from 4.0.3 (e.g. password length was V2.1.1 in 4.x and is 6.2.1 in 5.0); never reuse 4.x IDs. Use version-pinned IDs like v5.0.0-6.2.1.
Next planned release is patch 5.0.1. The 4.0-to-5.0 mapping notes (0x05-For-Users-Of-4.0.md) were not read.

Chapter summaries and prevention bullets are paraphrased from the L1 requirements in the notes; V16 and V17 have no requirement text in the notes, so their prevention lists are empty. detection entries are reinhardt heuristics; "(inferred) " related links are reinhardt mappings.

L1.description: Minimum requirements and critical starting point with a low barrier to entry; about 20% of requirements. Password rules weigh more here because MFA becomes relevant at higher levels. Not necessarily black-box testable. Suitable focus for e.g. an early-stage startup.

L2.description: The level most applications should strive for; adds about 50% of requirements, so L1+L2 is about 70%.

L3.description: For applications needing the highest security (e.g. a bank); the final ~30% of requirements.

id_format.note: Lowercase "v" prefix recommended for tools; unversioned IDs are assumed to refer to the latest version. Chapter items in this file use V1..V17.

items.name: Encoding and Sanitization
items.summary: Requirements for context-correct output encoding, injection-safe query and command construction, HTML sanitization, safe handling of dynamic code and safe XML parsing.
prevention: Encode output for its context (HTML, attributes, CSS, headers, JS/JSON, URLs).
Use parameterized queries or ORMs for SQL, HQL, NoSQL and Cypher.
Protect against OS command injection.
Sanitize WYSIWYG/HTML input with a known library and avoid eval-style dynamic code execution.
Disable XXE in XML parsers.

l1_requirements.summary: Context-relevant output encoding for HTML, attributes, CSS and headers.
URL building encodes untrusted data and allows only safe protocols (no javascript: or data:).
Encode untrusted data when building JavaScript or JSON.
Use parameterized queries or ORMs for SQL, HQL, NoSQL and Cypher.
Protect against OS command injection.
Sanitize WYSIWYG HTML input with a known library.
Avoid eval() and other dynamic code execution.
Configure XML parsers with XXE disabled.

static: SQL built with template literals or concatenation
eval / new Function / dynamic code execution
href built from user URLs without blocking javascript:/data: schemes
review: Correct encoding context selection in templates

items.name: Validation and Business Logic
items.summary: Requirements for documented, positive input validation enforced on a trusted service layer and for business flows that run in the expected order.
prevention: Document input validation rules.
Validate positively against business expectations.
Enforce validation on a trusted service layer; client-side validation is not a security control.
Process business flows in order without allowing steps to be skipped.

l1_requirements.summary: Input validation rules are documented.
Input is positively validated against business expectations.
Validation is enforced at a trusted service layer; client-side validation is not a security control.
Business flows are processed in order without skipping steps.

static: API handlers using req.body fields without a schema validator (zod/yup/joi/valibot) (heuristic)
Validation present only in client components
review: Whether documented rules exist and match implementation

items.name: Web Frontend Security
items.summary: Requirements for browser-side protections: rendering content in the right context, safe DOM APIs, cookie attributes, HSTS, CORS and CSRF defenses.
prevention: Prevent responses (uploads, API output) from rendering in an unintended context.
Use textContent/createTextNode for text rather than HTML sinks.
Set Secure and a __Host- or __Secure- prefix on cookies.
Send HSTS with max-age of at least one year on all responses.
Fix or allowlist the CORS Access-Control-Allow-Origin value.
Validate anti-CSRF tokens or rely on unbypassable preflight; use non-GET methods for sensitive actions.

l1_requirements.summary: Prevent content from rendering in the wrong context (e.g. directly requested uploads or API responses).
Use textContent/createTextNode when inserting text.
Cookies have the Secure attribute and a __Host- or __Secure- prefix.
HSTS is sent on all responses with max-age of at least one year.
CORS Access-Control-Allow-Origin is fixed or validated against an allowlist.
Anti-CSRF validation is performed when not relying on CORS preflight.
CORS preflight cannot be bypassed.
Sensitive actions use POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE, not GET.

static: Cookies without secure or name prefix

items.name: API and Web Service
items.summary: Requirements for API and web-service responses and transports, such as correct content types and secure WebSockets.
prevention: Return a correct Content-Type with charset on every response that has a body.
Use WSS for all WebSocket connections.

l1_requirements.summary: Every response with a body has a correct Content-Type including charset.
All WebSocket connections use WSS.

static: Responses sent without explicit content type (heuristic)
review: Content-type correctness across all endpoints at runtime

items.name: File Handling
items.summary: Requirements for limiting, validating, storing and serving uploaded files safely.
prevention: Enforce file size limits.
Validate extension and magic bytes, including files inside archives.
Never execute uploads stored in public folders server-side.
Use internally generated file paths, strictly validating any user-supplied filename.

l1_requirements.summary: File size limits are enforced.
File extension and magic-byte content are validated, including inside archives.
Uploads in public folders are never executed server-side.
Internally generated file paths are used; user filenames get strict validation against path traversal, LFI/RFI and SSRF.

static: Supabase Storage bucket created public: true for user uploads
review: Content validation depth for archives and images

items.name: Authentication
items.summary: Requirements for password policy, anti-automation, default accounts, credential lifecycle and recovery.
prevention: Require passwords of at least 8 characters (15 recommended) without composition rules or truncation.
Check new passwords against at least the top 3000 common passwords.
Implement brute-force and credential-stuffing controls.
Remove default accounts such as root, admin or sa.
Generate initial passwords and activation codes with a CSPRNG and keep them short-lived; no hints or secret questions.
Let users change their password (requiring the current one) and allow paste and password managers.

l1_requirements.summary: Anti-automation controls are documented.
Passwords are at least 8 characters (15 strongly recommended).
Users can change their password.
Password change requires the current password.
Passwords are checked against at least the top 3000 passwords.
No password composition rules are imposed.
Password fields use type=password.
Paste and password managers are allowed.
Passwords are not truncated or case-changed.
Brute-force and credential-stuffing controls are implemented.
No default accounts (e.g. root, admin, sa) exist.
Initial passwords and activation codes come from a CSPRNG and are short-lived.
No password hints or secret questions.

static: Password min length below 8 in validation schemas
No rate limiter on login/reset routes
Math.random for activation or reset codes

items.name: Session Management
items.summary: Requirements for backend-verified, dynamically generated, high-entropy session tokens and their rotation and invalidation.
prevention: Verify session tokens on a trusted backend.
Use dynamically generated session tokens rather than static API secrets.
Generate reference tokens with a CSPRNG and at least 128 bits of entropy.
Issue a new session token on authentication.
Make logout and expiry actually invalidate sessions, including a revocation approach for self-contained tokens; end sessions for disabled or deleted accounts.

l1_requirements.summary: Session tokens are verified on a trusted backend.
Session tokens are dynamically generated, not static API secrets.
Reference tokens come from a CSPRNG with at least 128 bits of entropy.
A new session token is issued on authentication.
Logout or expiry invalidates the session; self-contained tokens need a revocation solution.
Sessions are terminated when an account is disabled or deleted.

static: Static API keys used as session credentials in client code
Logout that only clears client state
review: Server-side invalidation on logout and account deletion

items.name: Authorization
items.summary: Requirements for documented authorization rules and function- and data-level access enforced on a trusted service layer.
prevention: Document authorization rules.
Restrict function-level access to explicit permissions.
Restrict data-specific access to prevent IDOR/BOLA.
Enforce authorization at a trusted service layer, never only in client-side code.

l1_requirements.summary: Authorization rules are documented.
Function-level access is restricted to explicit permissions.
Data-specific access is restricted (IDOR/BOLA).
Authorization is enforced at a trusted service layer, not client-side JavaScript.

static: Route handlers/Server Actions with DB access and no auth check
Queries by user-supplied ID without owner predicate
Role checks only in React/SwiftUI components
Supabase tables without RLS; Firebase rules without ownership

items.name: Self-contained Tokens
items.summary: Requirements for validating self-contained tokens such as JWTs: signature/MAC checks, algorithm allowlists, trusted key sources and validity windows.
prevention: Validate the signature or MAC before trusting token contents.
Use an algorithm allowlist and never accept "none".
Take key material only from trusted, pre-configured sources, validating jku, x5u and jwk headers.
Enforce nbf and exp claims.

l1_requirements.summary: Signature or MAC is validated before trusting token contents.
An algorithm allowlist is used and None is never allowed.
Key material comes from trusted, pre-configured sources (jku, x5u, jwk validated).
nbf and exp claims are enforced.

static: jwt.decode used for auth decisions instead of jwt.verify
jwt.verify without algorithms option or allowing 'none'

items.name: OAuth and OIDC
items.summary: Requirements for OAuth 2 and OpenID Connect clients and servers; the L1 items concern the authorization server (redirect URIs, codes, grants, refresh tokens).
prevention: Allowlist redirect URIs with exact matching.
Make authorization codes single-use with a lifetime of at most 10 minutes.
Do not use the implicit or password grants.
Mitigate refresh-token replay, for example with rotation.

l1_requirements.summary: Redirect URIs are validated against an exact-match allowlist.
Authorization codes are single-use.
Authorization code lifetime is at most 10 minutes (L1/L2).
Implicit and password grants are not used.
Refresh token replay is mitigated (rotation allowed at L1/L2).

static: OAuth client configs using response_type=token (implicit) or password grant
Wildcard redirect URI patterns in auth provider config files
review: Authorization-server behavior (code reuse, lifetimes, refresh rotation)

items.name: Cryptography
items.summary: Requirements for approved cipher modes, padding and hash functions.
prevention: Do not use ECB mode or PKCS#1 v1.5 padding.
Use approved ciphers such as AES-GCM.
Use approved hash functions only; never MD5 for any cryptographic purpose.

l1_requirements.summary: No ECB mode and no PKCS#1 v1.5 padding.
Only approved ciphers and modes such as AES-GCM.
Only approved hash functions; no MD5 for any cryptographic purpose.

items.name: Secure Communication
items.summary: Requirements for TLS versions and for using TLS with trusted certificates on all external HTTP services.
prevention: Allow only TLS 1.2 and 1.3.
Use TLS for all external HTTP services with no fallback to cleartext.
Use publicly trusted certificates for external services.

l1_requirements.summary: Only TLS 1.2 and 1.3 are enabled.
TLS is used for all external HTTP services with no fallback.
External services use publicly trusted certificates.

review: Live TLS versions and certificate chain

items.name: Configuration
items.summary: Requirements for secure configuration and secret management; at L1 only the requirement that source-control metadata is not deployed or reachable applies.
prevention: Ensure .git and .svn metadata is not deployed or accessible.
Manage secrets outside code per the V13 secret-management section (13.3.x, L2 and above).

l1_requirements.summary: No .git or .svn metadata is deployed or accessible.

static: .git or .svn directories inside public/ or build output

items.name: Data Protection
items.summary: Requirements for keeping sensitive data out of URLs and clearing authenticated data from client storage.
prevention: Never put sensitive data such as API keys or session tokens in URLs or query strings.
Clear authenticated data from client storage on logout (e.g. Clear-Site-Data).

l1_requirements.summary: Sensitive data (API keys, session tokens) never appears in URLs or query strings.
Authenticated data is cleared from client storage on logout (Clear-Site-Data).

static: Logout handlers that do not clear localStorage/cookies

items.name: Secure Coding and Architecture
items.summary: Requirements for managing vulnerable components within defined time frames and for minimizing data returned by the application.
prevention: Document remediation time frames for vulnerable components.
Keep components updated within those time frames.
Return only the required subset of fields instead of full objects.

l1_requirements.summary: Remediation time frames for vulnerable components are documented.
Components are kept within those remediation time frames.
Only the required subset of fields is returned (no full-object responses).

static: res.json(row) / select("*") returning full records to clients
review: Existence and adherence to remediation SLAs
